The site's widgets are written in JavaScript on top of dp-core, so they compute the model live
and work offline. Phase 10 tries four other routes to the same pictures and records when each is
worth it.

::: {.dpx-table-scroll tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Complementary tools and their status, scrollable table"}
| Catalog | Tool | Status | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| A-16 (and P-17) | gganimate videos (R, ffmpeg) | done | [Videos for talks](media.qmd) |
| X-02 | plotly animation frames and ggiraph hover (R htmlwidgets) | done | [The alpha sweep in plotly and ggiraph](dpprior/plotly-alpha-sweep.qmd) |
| X-01 | Observable Framework mini-site with an R data loader | waiting: needs `npm create @observablehq` (a new tool and network access), which the site owner has to approve | not built |
| C-17 | shinylive "Studio-lite" (the DPprior R code in the browser) | waiting: needs `install.packages("shinylive")` and `quarto add quarto-ext/shinylive`, which the site owner has to approve | not built; the hosted [DPprior Studio](https://joonho.shinyapps.io/dpprior-studio/) covers it meanwhile |
:::

What the two waiting studies would add: X-01 would show whether an Observable Framework site with
an R data loader is simpler to maintain than this Quarto site for a one-page explainer; C-17
would show the R package, Studio and the site's widgets giving the same Gamma(a, b) for the same
target, without a server.
